Gunnar 601 · machine and head calibration

Calibration sheet 2

A small offcut, raw from the machine: no profile and no trims are used to cut it. Eleven caliper readings on sharp or square edges and four checks by eye settle where each blade lands, how its slit falls, and how much overcut frees a corner on any thickness.

board 140 × 105 mm, 1.5 mmcuts 41, about 40 sreadings 11 + 4 by eye

The sheet, as it lies on the table

Which bevel edges to measure

Caliper readings

Mark the left and front edges of the offcut before lifting it. Push the two strips and the drop-out out. Measure at the middle of each edge.

ReadingAcrossFaceAbout
1SL.widthstraight strip SLeither10.0
2SR.widthstraight strip SReither10.0
3SL.lengthstraight strip SL, end to endeither25.0
4S.leftleft edge to the straight hole's left edgeeither28
5S.frontfront edge to the straight hole's front edgeeither28
6W.leftleft edge to the window's left edgeback67.5
7W.widththe window, left to rightback25.9
8W.frontfront edge to the window's front edgeback27.5
9W.heightthe window, front to backback25.9
10D.widththe loose drop-out, acrossface29.3
11D.heightthe loose drop-out, the other wayface29.3

The "about" values are where calibration 1 says each should land; the positions from the edges move with wherever the generator put the feature, which the fit allows for.

By eye, face up

Before turning the offcut over, pencil a 1 by tooth 1 of each comb: face up, the combs read in mirror image. Then find the first tooth, counting up from 1, whose slit reaches the comb's long reference slit.

AnswerCombTeeth 1 to 7, mm
12S.endstraight end comb: how far past the reference each tooth runs+0.6, +0.9, +1.2, +1.5, +1.8, +2.1, +2.4
13S.startstraight start comb: how far after the reference each tooth starts (negative)-2.7, -2.4, -2.1, -1.8, -1.5, -1.2, -0.9
14B.endbevel end comb+1.6, +1.9, +2.2, +2.5, +2.8, +3.1, +3.4
15B.startbevel start comb-0.9, -0.6, -0.3, 0.0, +0.3, +0.6, +0.9

Calibration 1 predicts the straight blade reaches from tooth 5 at the end and tooth 3 at the start, and the bevel from about tooth 3 at the end and tooth 4 at the start. If you can also see where the slits stop on the back, a note of that pins down the blade's edge angle.

What the readings settle

ReadingsSettle
1–3where each side of the straight slit falls, and the straight blade's tip off its turning axis, sideways
4–5where the straight blade lands from the stops, in carriage steps
6–9where the bevel blade lands from the stops, and the window's back edge
10–11the window's face edge, so the bevel's run from back to face
12–15each tip's position along the cut and its blade's depth × edge angle, which set the overcuts on any thickness

One command cuts it raw and then asks for each reading in turn, with its face and roughly what to expect; it fits them as soon as they are in:

gunnar calibrate cut
gunnar calibrate read        # later, or to correct a reading
gunnar calibrate fit --all   # every calibration session so far, together

The fit reads the exact carriage steps from the session's log, so it doesn't matter which profile was current. The readings, the fit and a profile with the fitted head offsets stay in the session folder (gunnar logs). Hooks, a trim row, belong on the per-board sheet.
